If sentiment is positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% in early horizon (1–7 days) to align with downward momentum.  
If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% in mid horizon (8–15 days) to counteract bearish bias.  
When sentiment swings from positive to negative over 3 consecutive days, shift forecast downward by 2–3% in late horizon (16–30 days) to reflect reversal risk.  
If sentiment is consistently neutral (0.33–0.67) over 5+ days, apply a 0.5–1.0% upward bias in early horizon to compensate for model inertia.  
In late horizon (16–30 days), if sentiment is positive but price has been trending downward for 7+ days, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.  
If sentiment is positive but forecast is consistently above true price for 5+ days, reduce forecast by 1–2% in mid horizon to prevent overoptimism.
